audit_findings.title: Roku financing makes the cash bridge and historical interest burden stale upon closing
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.205 billion cash add-back exposed, equal to 13.9% of $30.334 billion base equity or $9.60 per current share; exact cash use and incremental interest unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would reduce cash added in the equity bridge and add acquisition-debt interest to equity-level OE, while Roku earnings would also need inclusion.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to fund the cash portion of the Merger consideration with a combination of debt and cash on hand.
audit_findings.explanation: The last supplied filing describes the acquisition as pending, and the valuation explicitly uses the as-filed standalone perimeter, so no present error is demonstrated. Upon closing, retaining all cash and pre-merger interest expense could materially overstate standalone value unless the model simultaneously incorporates the purchase financing and Roku operations.
audit_findings.action: Confirm transaction status as of 2026-09-05; upon completion, rerun using the closing consideration, post-close cash and debt, actual financing rates, transaction shares and normalized Roku earnings.

audit_findings.title: Roku stock consideration is absent from the common-share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Merger shares and replacement awards would increase the fully diluted share denominator used to convert equity value into value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, FOX will pay $96.00 in cash and 0.9693 shares of FOX Class A Common Stock for each share of Roku Class A Common Stock and Roku Class B Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the merger.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is not an error in the pending-transaction, standalone valuation. If the merger closes, however, FOX must issue 0.9693 FOXA share for each outstanding Roku Class A and Class B share, potentially creating material dilution; the supplied record lacks Roku's transaction-date diluted share count, so the effect cannot be quantified.
audit_findings.action: At closing, obtain Roku shares outstanding, dilutive securities and replacement-award terms; calculate total FOXA issuance and rerun every per-share scenario with the post-close denominator.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved Smartmatic exposure could be a material claim on common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.7 billion claimed, equal to 8.9% of $30.334 billion base equity or $6.17 per share; probable loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unaccrued judgment or settlement would reduce common equity through the bridge and could also reduce future OE through defense costs.
audit_findings.evidence: This includes the lawsuit filed by Smartmatic USA Corp. and certain of its affiliates (collectively, “Smartmatic”) in February 2021 seeking $ 2.7 billion in damages.
audit_findings.explanation: No liability is demonstrated: FOX states that loss is neither probable nor reasonably estimable, and pleaded damages are not an estimate of likely loss. Nevertheless, the filed claim is large enough to change the conclusion—deducting the full pleaded amount would reduce base value from $69.29 to about $63.12 per share, below the $65.42 market price.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent rulings, trial status, settlement evidence, insurance and indemnification; develop supportable probability and loss-severity cases and rerun the equity bridge without treating pleaded damages as the expected loss.

audit_findings.title: Sports-rights amortization may not represent the normalized economic cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast-driven amortization timing enters operating expense and therefore historical OE, its trend-derived anchor and projected growth base.
audit_findings.evidence: Differing estimates of future revenues could materially affect the timing of sports programming amortization.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates estimation sensitivity, not an accounting error. Deferral could overstate current OE while acceleration could understate it. Total inventory amortization was $6.468 billion and licensed-programming commitments were $24.365 billion, but the record does not isolate the sports-rights timing difference or establish whether normalized OE is materially misstated.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile contract-level sports-rights cash payments, capitalized balances, attributable-revenue forecasts and amortization across the OE history; normalize major event cycles and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable minority interests are omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $86 million, equal to 0.28% of $30.334 billion base equity or $0.20 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The redemption claim should reduce the common-equity bridge if the OE numerator and consolidated assets include the affected subsidiaries.
audit_findings.evidence: Redeemable noncontrolling interests are presented outside of permanent equity on the Company’s Balance Sheets as their redemption is outside the control of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The $86 million balance-sheet claim is omitted, although the precise ownership consistency still depends on whether OE is parent-attributable. Even a full deduction would reduce base value only from $69.29 to about $69.09 per share and would not change the $48.50 buy threshold versus the $65.42 market price conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm subsidiary-level minority ownership and OE attribution, then deduct the applicable redemption value or value the related earnings and assets net of minority ownership in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: The stated dilution ceiling is not a true PSU maximum
audit_findings.magnitude: no more than 4.058 million additional shares, or 0.93% of the 437.809 million denominator; maximum base-value reduction about $0.64 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A 200% PSU payout adds shares above the target awards currently included in the fully diluted denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares that will be issued upon vesting of PSUs can range from 0 % to 200 % of the target award, based on the Company’s three-year total shareholder return (“TSR”) as measured against the three-year TSR of the companies that comprise the Standard and Poor’s 500 Index and other performance measures.
audit_findings.explanation: The ceiling label is demonstrably unsupported because the 4.058 million balance combines RSUs and target PSUs. Even assuming all 4.058 million units were PSUs and all earned the maximum additional 100%, base value would decline only from $69.29 to about $68.65 per share and the investment conclusion would remain unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the RSU-versus-PSU split and award-level maximum payouts from the proxy or compensation schedules, then replace the target-only amount with the true maximum denominator.
